chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Hawkins at a 52nd Street club; his friendship; Benny Carter's talent
summary: Thomas asks Hawkins to play 'Body and Soul' on 52nd Street, notes the money-minded Hawkins, and praises Benny Carter's natural writing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: But he was beautiful... And I went to one of the clubs on 52nd Street one night. That's when "Body and Soul" was popular. So I requested it. I said, "Coleman, would you play 'Body and Soul" for me?" He said, "Yeah." So he played it. And after he got... See, in them days I knew the so myself verbatim. Somebody even copied it off the record. But I heard it so much...
There were many ways to hear it.

And when he got through with it, I said, "You kind of ad-libbed on your own solo, didn't you?" He said, "You know I did." But I got to be very good friends with him. I got to know him well. And then before... I was so happy for me to ask him to record... Because he was a name,
he could have... He was a personality. He could have said no! All he wanted to know was how much money.
He was very much into money, wasn't he.

Yeah. A hundred dollars was just like paying for two guys. And he was worth two guys. But I remember it so distinctly... Because see, I didn't... I knew a lot about him when he went to Europe. But when you're in Europe, nobody know what you're doing. And everybody... All the saxophone players were just downin' him when he came back to New York City, like he's a has-been. You know, you can't keep up because you're in Europe. Shit... And I actually believe that he got wind of it, and that's when he went off all by himself and made "Body and Soul." And when "Body and Soul" came out, ain't nobody...!
Ain't nobody in town said nothin' else since then.

But Benny Carter has been my man for years. I was so anxious... With his talent... See, Benny Carter had this talent, and I was so anxious if he'd have studied... Because he's such a great writer. But he's just got that natural talent. I don't know where he got it from, but he's got it.
